title: The Rod and the Almond Blossom
english: …there are, they are fears. In general, the things proclaimed about the use confound the mind concerning such things; and especially when it is believed to be near, it confounds the mind and “amazement” results. They are amazed at the things said, and just as in sensible things, if a lightning strike is expected, all fear; when thunder comes, all are afraid. The psalmist said this too: “at the voice of your thunder they shall be afraid” (Ps 103:7). And just as from the sensible “voice” they take fear, being confounded, so from the loud-voiced divine word, about which it is said as of “thunder”: “the God of glory thundered” (Ps 28:3) and again “the Lord thundered from heaven” (2 Sam 22:14).

Those around James and John heard this “thunder”: for they were called “sons of thunder” (Mark 3:17). And as Peter, because of the firmness of the faith he had — the “rock” as it is called — was surnamed “Peter,” so these too were called “sons of thunder” from their loud voice. But perhaps someone will object to us: “Yes, let John thunder great things, theologizing and saying ‘In the beginning was the Word’ (John 1:1) and ‘he was the true light’ (John 1:9) and ‘the only-begotten God who is in the bosom of the Father’ (John 1:18); but what ‘thunder’ did James bring? For he was taken away at once.” We say that it can be said in a comprehensive way, or that both held loud-voiced things in mind, but James was not permitted to write, having been released quickly from life at the Savior’s assumption.

Just as from the sensible “thunder” “amazement” takes the hearers, and they fear through expectation or some other stroke, so when these heralds of the truth are “lifted up,” “amazement” takes those still “on the way”; but they must already be those who have ascended to the “height.” “And the almond shall blossom” (Eccl 12:5). Those who have spoken about the nature of plants say this about the “almond”: before all plants in spring it puts forth leaves and casts them off after the casting-off of all the other trees; it is lasting, then. For this reason the priestly “rod” was said to be of “almond-wood” (Num 17:23). For it did not remain for a few days: from Moses until the visitation of the Savior it appeared.

They were deacons of these traditions. And they quickly 'flourished' and quickly withered. But the priestly 'rod' of 'almond-wood,' being so, remained for long, until a succession might be born from the greater and more spiritual priesthood; and it blossomed before the others. And this must be said: that there will be a true teaching and a false and deceptive one. For they say: in the times of the prophets, false prophets are found; for the evil is a mimic of the true. From the time that Christ appeared in visitation, many false Christs promised to come.

We say therefore this: even if those of the other teachings were plants, and later 'blossom' after the upright teaching and before it; for when it appears, they are quenched. This 'rod' therefore loosed the 'rods' of the others, of the false apostles, of the false prophets. Will the 'almond' therefore 'blossom'?—this: when 'the daughters of the song are humbled' (Song of Solomon), the promised false teachings, false 'rods', then even more 'the almond will blossom'.

Regarding the apostolic word, we say that there will be a standing of righteousness when injustice prevails among men. Loosing the injustice and revealing those who advocate it, being something great, its greatness would not have been shown if there were not a great injustice which it loosed. And we say that 'the truth of God prevailed in human falsehood'. And we say that then, especially, the good appeared of the truth, when many false sophists came into the midst, promising contentious words.

Let there be a king capable and having a many-handed army and experienced in war. Does his greatness not appear when he goes against an enemy of thirty men and prevails over them? And not thus by the Preacher, but rather by Ezra, were problems regarding the king set forth. And the former two have spoken well, but the second interpretation of the third was strong; and it has been said that 'truth conquers' and is powerful. For even if 'women are strong' and such 'wine' and the 'king' and the others, but 'truth excels'. The 'prevailing' of the 'truth' appeared while those strong ones were present.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Human as a Dwelling and the Response to the Flute
english: Having been interpreted by others, they were somewhat obscure, remembering; and remembering this, the magnitude of the 'truth' did not appear. And the 'acris' (judgment) might grow fat. In the apostolic [word] it was said again this: that where there is 'law', there also is 'transgression'. If the gospel had not come into the midst, there would not have been a great punishment according to those not receiving it.

Immediately indeed he says that it is necessary 'that this gospel of the kingdom be preached in all the world for a testimony to all the nations' (Matt 24:14), so that no one might take a pretext to seize the unseemly. When therefore the aforementioned 'almond shall blossom', the 'acris' (judgment) 'grows fat'; and the 'acris' is taken instead of a flogging; 'the locusts consumed the remnant of the field' (Joel 1:4). And it 'grows fat' then receiving much food; and its food are the men being handed over to it. And it is possible also to take as a character the 'blossoming of the almond'.

The 'almond' has two perimeters outside the edible part: shell-like and then bitter, the husk which is on the outside. The outside husk may be the body; for it is bitter, having a relation to pleasure. But that shell-like husk is the soul, for it is well-proportioned and large; and within is the edible, the spirit. When therefore that [thing] of the time of the apostle writing is fulfilled: 'May the God of peace sanctify you wholly, your whole spirit and soul and body' (1 Thess 5:23), 'the almond has blossomed'; for in the 'blossoming' these three things are contained. Therefore the man 'blossoms' when he advances in virtue, having 'the body being transformed' (Rom 12:2) so as to become 'conformed' to the 'body' of Christ.

And the caparis might be scattered, because the man went into the house of his age. The 'house of the age' of the 'man' is the life after these things. All the things spoken are happening: and 'the doors are shut in the marketplace', and 'they rise up to the voice of the sparrow' (Prov 7:23) those being called to this, and 'the daughters of the singer are humbled' (Ps 84:12). Those who are in the 'house' of the 'age' are the 'men'. And the place concerning the earth is the 'house' of this 'age of the evil one'. All the things spoken are happening. Since therefore [he] 'went into' another 'age', [he went] 'into' the age of 'his own house', 'into' that after these things.

All things having passed away here are loosed. It is possible to take it this way also, since the 'man' is according to the soul. When all the things that have come to him are loosed—the fleeting things, the trivial things—he 'goes into' his own remaining 'house,' having left this 'age.' And an 'age' is appropriate and a 'house' is for the 'man' who has become a divine state, being 'according to the image and likeness of God,' from which he 'departed' from this 'age.' Those things are loosed, as if someone says that fornication has ceased. For the 'man departed into' the place of incorruption.

And those being cut in mourning surrounded [him] in the marketplace (Matt 12:5). Therefore, 'after the flute has been played' and 'the wailing' is increasing, those formerly speaking in the marketplace, as if lamenting them, [speak]. Therefore, 'in the marketplace those being cut surrounded [him].' You also have it said in the Gospel by the Savior: 'To what generation shall I liken this generation?' and he says: 'It is like children sitting in the marketplace, calling to one another: We played the flute for you and you did not dance; we mourned for you and you did not weep' (Matt 11:17). And he adds: 'John came neither eating nor drinking' (Matt 11:10). Behold the 'lamenting of the child'; for John is taken for all the ancient Scripture and those who ministered to it, but the Son of Man [is taken] for the body of the Church, the apostolic and evangelical choir. He says, therefore, that the 'children play the flute,' so it is necessary for those hearing the flute to 'dance.' But the 'dancing' of the imitation of words is promised to be made through the hands. When, therefore, they hear the word of the wise of salvation and the word bringing forth piety, and are conformed to the announced works and the intellect, they 'dance' praiseworthily according to the dancing which David 'danced' before the ark (2 Sam 6:14). For when they 'lament' calling to repentance, raising up feeling, they 'cut [their breasts],' because this raises up feeling. When one laments and cuts [his breast] because another is sinning, he immediately says, 'How much this one reproaches himself for my sake, I also ought to do this.' And these, therefore, hearing the lament, if they 'cut [their breasts]' bearing their hands against their chests, they raise up feeling for themselves. These, therefore, [were] the former speakers...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Marketplace and the Silver Cord
english: And having said many things regarding those who do not listen, they 'are being cut'. Thus also Jeremiah, after Israel and Jerusalem had been taken captive, having sat in desolation, lamented with a wail for the throne. And even so God says: 'Lament for me concerning the bride girded with a sackcloth for her man, the virgin conquering'. Therefore, 'those being cut were surrounding in the marketplace'. The teachers rejoice when the hearers are being made straight; they are grieved when the divine decrees are heard against them. Since, therefore, even after the hearers sin, the teachers pity them in proclaiming the divine, 'those being cut cry out', not seeing those who are doing what they stand in defense of. And the New Testament knows the church as a 'marketplace', just as the Greeks do. In the Acts of the Apostles, indeed, it says that 'they have' certain requests, 'market-people lead them', that is to say, rhetoricians. 'You are able', he says, 'to move a case concerning this, those who are proclaiming, the rhetoricians'. Therefore, 'those being cut surrounded in the marketplace' those who were proclaiming; having been exalted and even 'dancing' after 'having surrounded', [it would be] 360 if what is said by them were being transferred into works of ages. Before the silver cord is overturned and the golden ornament is crushed.

12,6ab Toward a literal sense: 'the silver cord' may be the giving and the receiving concerning transactions. Toward a spiritual sense: since the word of the Lord is 'silver' and 'his words are refined silver', 'cords' are woven from these; that is, things well-understood by the orthodox or otherwise, both ways, the 'silver cord is not overturned', [it] 'is active'. But since we must speak according to the text, this can be said: that “while the silver cord” “is active” — not “being overturned,” not “being cast out” (for it “shall be cast out” after these things, when “that which is in part is abolished” [1 Cor 13:10]) — “those being cut in the marketplace surround,” “while” they have the “silver cord,” “while” they weave the “oracles of the Lord”; for then they also proclaim.
12,6b And the golden ornament is crushed. The deposit of 'gold' is so called, perhaps also the 'gold' itself, but rather the deposit. For those guarding the treasure neglect...

“Gold,” then, must be taken here as the mind; and “silver” as the uttered word. “Gold” you take here as the meaning, and “flower-ornament” as the ruling part, as being the case and guard of the “gold.” And if “silver” signifies the word and the scripture of God, it is a weaving to take fitting sayings with fitting ones, and to join the understanding of these to those and of those to these. Again: does he not mean the church by “until”? — he means this: “in the marketplace those being cut are cut as they surround.” “Marketplace” is the ecclesiastical teaching. And by ecclesiastical I do not mean altogether that of the Christians, but the congregational. This, then, is what he says: that as long as the “silver cord” “is active,” they “surround” and “lament” the disobedient.

But when it “is overturned,” “when that which is in part is abolished” (1 Cor 13:10), no longer do “those being cut surround the marketplace”; for their lamentation will no longer effect anything then, when each hears: “now you repent, when there is no ‘time.’” But I do not say this, that there will never be repentance, but then, when the “time of judgment” is active, when “they stand before the judgment seat of Christ, that each may receive what he did through the body” (2 Cor 5:10). Again: but if it “is not overturned”? — this: then “those being cut surround in the marketplace,” while the word of the teaching is still “active,” though they are not persuaded, not assenting, not bound by the “silver cord”; for the one who assents is bound.

“And the flower-ornament is crushed.” It was said that scripture signifies the meanings by “gold”; the meanings, then, worked out and prepared so as to become good oracles. For “petals” appear, cut in the garments of the high priest; for it is said […] “gold” and the lower construction […]. It can, then, “be crushed” […] to join them together and as it were to be hammered flat. “And the pitcher is shattered at the spring, and the wheel runs together at the cistern” (Eccl 12:6). It belongs to some to drink from the “spring” itself without the vessel. Rebekah — the perseverance in good things, the perfect teaching — “going down to the spring,” took the drink “with a pitcher,” that […].
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
